title: Soyuz-2.1b Progress MS-36 (97P, Baikonur 31/6)

pad.src: https://ll.thespacedevs.com/2.3.0/launches/8dd5de11-831b-445f-86f0-bffefe0550d9/ (pad 31/6). Elevation is not on that record; 0 m is an ASSUMPTION.

azimuth_deg.assumption: No Baikonur hazard polygon for 24 Nov 2026 05:03Z was found. 63.39 deg is the non-rotating northeast azimuth for a 51.6 deg inclination from this pad: sin(az)=cos(51.6)/cos(45.996034). The southeast supplement (116.61 deg) was not used; Progress ISS launches head northeast. Not retuned after the sim. RussianSpaceWeb's prior Progress insertions were 51.67 deg, not 51.6.

payload_kg.assumption: Wikipedia Progress MS-36 lists a launch mass of 7,280 kg and cites Next Spaceflight. That page also says Soyuz-2.1a, 09:03 UTC and a Zvezda docking, which disagree with LL2 (05:03Z, Soyuz-2.1b) and with Poisk. No Roscosmos mass for this ship was found. 7,280 kg is used as that Wikipedia figure and is not a weighed MS-36 mass. Fixed, not fitted.

insertion_alt_km.assumption: MS-36 insertion elements are unpublished. 193 km perigee is borrowed from Progress MS-19 (193 x 240 km) and Progress MS-27 (193.2 x 239.8 km), both Soyuz-2.1a. https://www.russianspaceweb.com/progress-ms-19.html https://www.russianspaceweb.com/progress-ms-27.html

apoapsis_alt_km.assumption: Apogee borrowed from the same Progress MS-19 / MS-27 parking orbits. Not an MS-36 source. The ISS altitude is not the insertion orbit.

target.altitude_reference: equatorial-radius (r - 6378.137 km) for SMA; insertion altitude residual uses geodetic altitude

header_notes: ILLUSTRATIVE. Progress MS-36 (97P), Baikonur Site 31/6, T0 2026-11-24T05:03:00Z. LL2 id 8dd5de11-831b-445f-86f0-bffefe0550d9, status To Be Confirmed, net precision Minute, window start=end 05:03Z, last_updated 2026-06-08T21:46:36Z. Next Spaceflight lists the same 05:03Z.

VEHICLE CONFLICT, not silent: this file flies Soyuz-2.1b (RD-0124). LL2 and Next Spaceflight name Soyuz-2.1b. Interfax, dateline 22 September with no year printed, quotes Roscosmos: Soyuz-2.1b was adapted for Progress MS, the first such launch was 16 September, and Soyuz-2.1a continues for satellites and crewed flights (https://www.interfax.ru/russia/1117752). Roscosmos TV http://www.tvroscosmos.ru/2833/ lists Progress MS-36 from Baikonur 31 on 24 Nov 2026 and does not name 2.1a or 2.1b. Wikipedia EN says Soyuz-2.1a, 09:03 UTC and Zvezda aft. Prior Progress flights cited here (MS-19, MS-23, MS-27, MS-28) flew Soyuz-2.1a.

Event times and the 193 x 240 km parking orbit are BORROWED from those Soyuz-2.1a flights. No MS-36 or Soyuz-2.1b Progress timeline was found. Docking target is Poisk (task / Next Spaceflight class of reports). Wikipedia says Zvezda. Docking is not modelled.

Stage-3 cutoff is ignition 286.159 s plus Wikipedia's 270 s RD-0124 burn (556.159 s). The Soyuz-2.1a cutoff 525.45 s and the 8 min 49 s separation are recorded and are not the hard events: that shorter burn left this model suborbital. Separation is 4 s after the 2.1b cutoff (560.159 s), the same gap as MS-19's 525.45 s to 529 s.

final_cutoff_s.derived: Borrowed Stage III ignition 286.159 s (Progress MS-19) plus Wikipedia's generic Soyuz-2.1b RD-0124 burn of 270 s (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz-2). The MS-19 cutoff 525.45 s is a Soyuz-2.1a RD-0110 time. Using it on RD-0124 in this model shut down 31 s early and the fit could not reach orbit (161 km, flight-path angle -1.5 deg, perigee below the surface). That 2.1a clock is recorded and is not the hard cutoff.

knots.src: https://www.russianspaceweb.com/progress-ms-19.html altitude of around 43 km. Range not published.

knots.event: Fairing separation (Progress MS-19 altitude, MS-27 range)
knots.src: https://www.russianspaceweb.com/progress-ms-19.html about 91 km; https://www.russianspaceweb.com/progress-ms-27.html around 200 km downrange. Both around-figures, both Soyuz-2.1a.

knots.event: Core separation (Progress MS-19 altitude, MS-27 range)

cd.assumption: Free-molecular Cd. The coast from cutoff to separation is about 4 s, so the value barely moves the state.

area_m2.derived: pi*(2.66 m/2)^2 from the Block I diameter on https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soyuz-2

t_s.derived: 2.1b cutoff 556.159 s plus 4 s. The 4 s is the gap from Progress MS-19 cutoff 525.45 s to the prose separation at 8 min 49 s (529 s). https://www.russianspaceweb.com/progress-ms-19.html The absolute 529 s is the 2.1a flight's separation and is not this file's deploy time. RIA on Progress MS-28 also says 8 min 49 s (https://ria.ru/20240815/korabl-1966304630.html).
